messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] 5101010101 - Streaming API latency SLO breach detected. p95=2.1s (baseline ~150ms), p99=14.8s. Spike started ~06:12:31Z. Affected cluster: gpu-pool-eu-west-2. Auto-fallbacks not triggering as expected. Paging on-call: @alice, runtime: @raj, infra: @susan. Impact: streaming token stalls >30s for some sessions.

alice: On it. I'm pulling graphs. Has hardware been paged yet?

raj: I'm in metrics now. KV cache hit rate dropped 94% -> 18% on one node (gpu42). nvml shows thermal oscillation and ECC correctable errors rising. NVLINK link resets present.

liz: Seeing repeated token emission stalls in traces. Some clients show partial responses then long pauses. Affects ~8 tenants (2 Dedicated).

jamie: @susan can you confirm node-side health? If this is ECC/thermal we should drain and failover asap.

susan: SSH'd to gpu42, running quick checks. Snippet: ```bash
ssh infra@gpu42
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,clocks.sm,fan.speed,ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv
# sample output:
# 92, 1815, 100, 127
# ecc.corrected counter jumping rapidly
```

susan: Also seeing kernel dmesg lines: "GPU fault: R/W timeout" and NVLINK resets.

raj: Correlating traces: KV cache flush events line up with NVLINK resets. Runtime goes into a recompilation path which amplifies tail latency — looks like a "vaporlock" pattern (hardware-induced stall -> runtime amplification).

alice: I'll route new streaming sessions off gpu-pool-eu-west-2 to fallback cluster and enable aggressive prefix warmup. Command: `/ops route set --cluster gpu-pool-eu-west-2 --fallback-cluster gpu-pool-eu-west-2-fallback --mode immediate`

alice: Also toggled runtime to disable multi-GPU aggregation for streaming on that node group: ```json
PATCH /runtime/config
{ "gpu_enable_multi_agg": false }
```

eric: Support: notifying the two Dedicated customers now. One reported ~25s spinner, other saw duplication. CSM looped.

tony: PM: do we expect customer-visible downtime if we drain the node? Need to prep banner.

liz: If we drain gpu42, sessions should reconnect to fallback with ~5-12s transient reconnects. That's better than repeated 30s+ stalls.

susan: Initiating drain: `kubectl drain gpu42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=2m`. Monitoring now.

deploy-bot: rolling update started for node drain handler (evicting pods) on gpu42 at 06:14:02Z.

raj: Evictions in progress. Also raised per-connection token timeout to 45s to reduce retry churn while reconnects happen.

alice: Owners: @susan hardware remediation and quarantine, @raj runtime triage and trace collection, @liz postmortem draft and timeline, @eric customer comms, @jamie fallback capacity.

jamie: Scaling fallback pool +2 GPUs now. Resize in progress (~3m).

susan: Drain completed. Node marked Unschedulable. Power-cycling and running ECC/memtest. If counters persist we'll quarantine and replace.

raj: After failover, p95 dropped to ~180ms and p99 to ~1.2s within 90s. Streaming stall rate down from ~5.9% -> 0.8%. KV cache warmups succeeding on fallback.

alice: Good mitigation. Keep gpu42 quarantined until hardware clears.

liz: Customer update sent: "We're mitigating an infrastructure issue affecting streaming latency; affected sessions are recovering. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

eric: Two customers acknowledged. No SLA credit request so far.

alice: Next actions: hardware forensic (susan), full runtime trace capture and analysis (raj), postmortem with timeline + follow-ups (liz). Target: initial RCA draft in 48h.

susan: Attaching syslog snippet showing repeated thermal trip entries + NVLINK resets between 06:11:58Z-06:13:12Z.

raj: Saved runtime traces to: /var/log/serving/runtime-traces/5101010101.tar.gz. Will upload to incident bucket.

alice: Marking incident mitigated for now. Moving to follow-up. :white_check_mark:

jamie: :thumbsup:

liz: :eyes:

eric: :handshake:
